strengths: Strong, consistent 'Abyssal Glow' deep-sea theme: a glowing teal/cyan board, low-poly rocks around the edge, swaying seagrass, glowing orbs and a pink jellyfish as the food
Polished glass-style HUD (Score/Level/Best), a styled title card with key hints, a Game Over screen with a 'NEW BEST!' badge, and a sound toggle
The snake is a modeled creature that looks like an axolotl, with gills and a tapering tail, not a chain of cubes
Bloom is used well: the edge lights, orbs and jellyfish glow without washing out the scene
Pink shockwave ring when eating, which grows between 100 ms and 450 ms
Movement looks smooth between frames; all 13/13 browser checks pass, no page errors, and the autopilot ate 22 foods in 40 s
Portrait phone layout adapts: the board fits, the title card sits below it, and swipe controls are shown
weaknesses: The snake and food are tiny compared with the large empty board, so they are hard to read, especially at the far, top edge where most of the action in the screenshots happens
The grid floor has a dense cyan texture that pulls attention away from the snake
No visible shadows under the snake or the food to anchor them to the floor
The camera is fixed in every frame; no dynamic camera work is shown
The eating effect is only a single ring; no particles or snake reaction are visible
The Game Over panel covers the lower half of the board
oneLine: A polished, atmospheric deep-sea snake with a cohesive HUD and a charming creature, held back by a tiny, hard-to-read snake on a huge busy board and a static camera.
